projectCategory: DSA Module 7.1: Graph Representations & Traversal Algorithms Architecture
subject: Data Structures & Algorithms in C

projects.title: Graph Adjacency Matrix Data Structure in C
projects.description: An Adjacency Matrix represents a graph of V vertices as a 2D 0/1 grid `int adj[V][V]`. Element `adj[u][v] = 1` indicates an edge between vertex `u` and `v`. Edge lookups take instant O(1) time, but memory consumption is `O(V^2)`. In this project, you will build an Adjacency Matrix Graph Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 2D Matrix Graph Representations, Instant O(1) Edge Lookups & O(V^2) Memory Tradeoffs
projects.exampleText: Build adjacency matrix for 4 vertices and query edge existence
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Graph Adjacency Matrix ---
Edge (0,1): 1, Edge (0,2): 0
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Matrix Initialization**: Set all cells in `adj[V][V]` to 0.
2. **Edge Addition**: Set `adj[u][v] = 1` and `adj[v][u] = 1` (for undirected graph).
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `init_matrix()` & `add_edge_matrix()`: Manages graph representation using Adjacency Matrix.

projects.title: Graph Adjacency List Data Structure with Dynamic Allocation
projects.description: An Adjacency List represents a graph of V vertices using an array of linked lists `Node *head[V]`. Vertex `u` contains a linked list of all its neighboring vertices. Reduces memory consumption from `O(V^2)` down to optimal `O(V + E)` for sparse graphs! In this project, you will build Dynamic Adjacency List Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Adjacency List Data Structures, Dynamic Node Pointer Allocation & O(V + E) Memory Optimization
projects.exampleText: Build adjacency list for 4 vertices and print neighbors of 0
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Graph Adjacency List ---
Neighbors of 0: 2 1
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Head Array**: Initialize array of pointers `head[V]` to NULL.
2. **List Prepend**: Prepend newly created neighbor node to `head[u]` linked list.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `create_graph_list()` & `add_edge_list()`: Manages graph representation using dynamic Adjacency List.

projects.title: Breadth-First Search (BFS) Traversal Engine
projects.description: Breadth-First Search (BFS) explores a graph level by level in concentric circles starting from a source node using a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) Queue. Guarantees finding the shortest path (unweighted minimum edge count) in O(V + E) time! In this project, you will build BFS Traversal Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: BFS Level-Order Traversal, FIFO Queue Operations & Unweighted Shortest Path Guarantees
projects.exampleText: Traverse 5-node graph using BFS queue
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Breadth-First Search (BFS) Traversal Engine ---
BFS Level Traversal Order: [ 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **FIFO Queue**: Enqueue source node; mark `visited[source] = true`.
2. **Level Expansion**: Pop front node `u`, iterate all unvisited neighbors `v`, mark visited and enqueue.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bfs_demo()`: Solves graph level-order traversal using BFS.

projects.title: Depth-First Search (DFS) Traversal Engine (Recursive)
projects.description: Depth-First Search (DFS) explores a graph by diving as deep as possible down each branch before backtracking using recursion / call stack. Operates in O(V + E) time and O(V) stack space. In this project, you will build Recursive DFS Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: DFS Branch Exploration, Call Stack Backtracking & Graph Traversal Guarantees
projects.exampleText: Traverse 5-node graph using recursive DFS
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Depth-First Search (DFS) Traversal Engine ---
DFS Path Traversal Order: [ 0, 1, 3, 4, 2 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Recursive Visit**: Mark current node `u` as visited.
2. **Branch Deepening**: Recurse on each unvisited neighbor `v` immediately.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `dfs_demo()`: Solves depth-first graph traversal using recursion.

projects.title: Iterative DFS Traversal using Explicit Stack
projects.description: System call stack overhead can cause stack overflow exceptions on huge deep graphs. Implement DFS iteratively using an EXPLICIT stack data structure `int stack[MAXV]`, preventing stack overflow in O(V + E) time! In this project, you will build Iterative Stack DFS Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Iterative DFS Mechanics, Explicit LIFO Stack Management & Stack Overflow Prevention
projects.exampleText: Traverse graph iteratively using explicit LIFO stack
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Iterative DFS Traversal using Explicit Stack ---
Iterative Stack DFS Order: [ 0, 2, 4, 1, 3 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Explicit Stack**: Push source node onto explicit stack array.
2. **LIFO Loop**: Pop top node `u`, mark visited, and push unvisited neighbors onto stack.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `iterative_dfs_demo()`: Executes non-recursive DFS using an explicit LIFO stack.

projects.title: Detect Cycle in Directed Graph (DFS 3-Coloring: White, Gray, Black)
projects.description: Detect if a directed graph contains a cycle using 3-Coloring DFS: 1) **WHITE (0)** = Unvisited; 2) **GRAY (1)** = Visiting (currently in recursion stack); 3) **BLACK (2)** = Fully visited. Encapsulates back-edges: encountering a GRAY neighbor during DFS proves a CYCLE exists! In this project, you will build Directed Graph Cycle Detector in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Directed Cycle Proofs, 3-Coloring DFS States & Back-Edge Detection
projects.exampleText: Detect cycle in directed graph via 3-coloring DFS
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Detect Cycle in Directed Graph (DFS 3-Coloring) ---
Cycle Detected via Back-Edge (Gray -> Gray): YES
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Set Gray**: Mark `color[u] = GRAY` before exploring neighbors.
2. **Back-Edge Test**: If neighbor `v` is `GRAY`, cycle detected! Mark `color[u] = BLACK` when exiting.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `cycle_directed_dfs_demo()`: Solves directed cycle detection using 3-Coloring DFS.

projects.title: Topological Sort via Kahn's Algorithm (BFS Indegree Queue)
projects.description: Topological Sort linearly orders vertices of a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) such that for every directed edge `u -> v`, vertex `u` comes before `v`. Kahn's algorithm computes `indegree[v]` for all nodes. Enqueue all 0-indegree nodes into BFS queue; decrement indegrees during traversal in O(V + E) time! In this project, you will build Kahn's Topological Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Kahn's BFS Topological Sort, Indegree Counting & DAG Dependency Resolution
projects.exampleText: Sort DAG vertices topologically via Kahn's BFS algorithm
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Topological Sort via Kahn's Algorithm (BFS Indegree) ---
Topological Order: [ 5, 4, 2, 3, 1, 0 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Indegree Queue**: Enqueue all vertices with `indegree[i] == 0`.
2. **Indegree Decrement**: Pop node `u`, append to result list; decrement `indegree[v]` for neighbors. Enqueue if indegree becomes 0.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `topo_kahns_demo()`: Computes topological sorting using Kahn's BFS algorithm.

projects.title: Topological Sort via DFS Post-Order Stack
projects.description: Compute topological order of a DAG using DFS: recurse down branches to terminal nodes, then push nodes onto a result stack upon returning (Post-Order DFS traversal). Pop stack to yield valid topological order in O(V + E) time! In this project, you will build DFS Topological Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: DFS Post-Order Traversal, Stack Reversal Mechanics & DAG Ordering Invariants
projects.exampleText: Sort DAG vertices topologically via DFS post-order stack
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Topological Sort via DFS Post-Order Stack ---
Topological Order (DFS Stack): [ 5, 4, 2, 3, 1, 0 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **DFS Traversal**: Recurse on all unvisited neighbors.
2. **Post-Order Push**: Push node `u` onto stack ONLY AFTER all its dependencies have been processed.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `topo_dfs_demo()`: Solves topological sorting using DFS post-order stack.

projects.title: Bipartite Graph Detection using BFS / 2-Coloring
projects.description: Check if an undirected graph is Bipartite (vertices can be partitioned into 2 sets such that no two adjacent vertices share the same color). Run BFS and color vertices with alternating colors (1 and 2). If adjacent vertices have the SAME color, graph is NOT bipartite! In this project, you will build Bipartite BFS Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Graph 2-Coloring, BFS Alternating Colors & Bipartite Proofs
projects.exampleText: Verify 2-colorability of undirected graph via BFS
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Bipartite Graph Detection via BFS 2-Coloring ---
Is Graph Bipartite (2-Colorable): YES
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Color Flip**: Assign `color[v] = 3 - color[u]` for adjacent neighbors.
2. **Conflict Check**: If neighbor already colored with `color[v] == color[u]`, return false.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bipartite_bfs_demo()`: Validates graph bipartite property via BFS 2-coloring.

projects.title: Number of Connected Components in Undirected Graph
projects.description: Count total connected components in an undirected graph using BFS/DFS traversals. Loop through all vertices `0 .. V-1`: whenever an unvisited vertex is encountered, launch a new traversal and increment `component_count++` in O(V + E) time! In this project, you will build Component Traversal Counter in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Outer Vertex Loop Traversals, Disjoint Island Counting & O(V + E) Full Graph Sweeps
projects.exampleText: Count connected components in undirected graph
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Connected Components Count in Undirected Graph ---
Total Connected Components = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Outer Loop**: Loop `i` from `0` to `V-1`.
2. **Launch Traversal**: If `!visited[i]`, launch BFS/DFS and increment `component_count++`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `connected_components_traversal_demo()`: Counts connected components via graph traversal.

projects.title: Flood Fill Algorithm (2D Grid BFS / DFS)
projects.description: Given a 2D image grid, starting pixel `(sr, sc)`, and a new color, perform a 'paint bucket' flood fill by updating all 4-directionally connected pixels matching original color to new color using Grid BFS/DFS in O(R * C) time! In this project, you will build Flood Fill Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Grid 4-Directional Traversals, Image Paint Bucket Fill & O(R*C) Matrix Sweeps
projects.exampleText: Execute 4-directional flood fill on 2D grid
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Flood Fill Algorithm (2D Grid Traversal) ---
Grid filled with target color 2 starting from cell (1,1).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Color Match**: Verify neighbor cell has original starting color.
2. **4-Direction Step**: Move to `(r+1,c), (r-1,c), (r,c+1), (r,c-1)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `flood_fill_demo()`: Solves 2D grid flood fill algorithm.

projects.title: Number of Islands (Grid BFS / DFS Traversal)
projects.description: Given an `R x C` binary grid of '1's (land) and '0's (water), count total islands (connected 4-directional land components). Iterate through grid: launch DFS/BFS from each unvisited '1' to sink the island (turn '1's to '0's) in O(R * C) time! In this project, you will build Number of Islands Grid Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Grid Component Sinking, Land Boundary Exploration & O(R*C) Matrix Traversal
projects.exampleText: Count 4-directional land islands on 2D grid
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Number of Islands (Grid BFS / DFS Traversal) ---
Total Islands Count on Grid = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Grid Scan**: Loop through all grid cells `(r, c)`.
2. **Island Sinking**: If `grid[r][c] == '1'`, launch DFS/BFS to set all connected land to '0' and increment count.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `number_of_islands_grid_demo()`: Solves Number of Islands via 2D grid traversal.

projects.title: Rotting Oranges (Multi-Source BFS on 2D Grid)
projects.description: Given grid with fresh oranges (1) and rotten oranges (2), every minute any fresh orange 4-directionally adjacent to a rotten orange rots. Find minimum minutes until no fresh oranges remain. Enqueue ALL initial rotten oranges simultaneously into a **Multi-Source BFS Queue** in O(R * C) time! In this project, you will build Rotting Oranges Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Multi-Source BFS Initializations, Simultaneous Level Expansion & Grid Time Metrics
projects.exampleText: Find minimum minutes to rot all oranges via Multi-Source BFS
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Rotting Oranges (Multi-Source BFS on 2D Grid) ---
Minutes elapsed until all oranges rot = 4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Multi-Source Queue**: Enqueue all initially rotten oranges into BFS queue.
2. **Minute Rounds**: Process level by level; increment `minutes++` after expanding each queue level.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `rotting_oranges_demo()`: Solves Rotting Oranges problem using Multi-Source BFS.

projects.title: Clone Graph (Deep Copy with HashMap Node Lookup)
projects.description: Given a reference node of a connected undirected graph, create a DEEP COPY (clone) of the entire graph. Use BFS/DFS traversal combined with a HashMap `old_node -> new_node` lookup table to clone nodes and reconstruct adjacency links in O(V + E) time! In this project, you will build Clone Graph Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Graph Deep Copy Mechanics, Node Mapping HashTables & Cyclic Reference Clones
projects.exampleText: Deep copy graph with HashMap node lookup
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Clone Graph (Deep Copy with HashMap Node Lookup) ---
Cloned 4 graph nodes with original adjacency structures preserved.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **HashMap Lookup**: Store created clones in `map[old_node] = clone_node`.
2. **Adjacency Copy**: Attach cloned neighbor pointers to `clone_node->neighbors` list.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `clone_graph_demo()`: Solves Clone Graph using BFS/DFS with HashMap lookup.

projects.title: Word Ladder (Shortest Transformation Sequence BFS)
projects.description: Given beginWord, endWord, and wordList, find length of shortest transformation sequence changing 1 letter at a time where every intermediate word exists in wordList. Model words as graph vertices and single-letter differences as edges. BFS guarantees shortest path in `O(N * L^2)` time! In this project, you will build Word Ladder Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Implicit Word Graphs, Single-Letter Transitions & Shortest Path BFS Guarantees
projects.exampleText: Find shortest transformation sequence from 'hit' to 'cog'
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Word Ladder (Shortest Transformation Sequence BFS) ---
Shortest Transformation Length from 'hit' to 'cog' = 5
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Implicit Edges**: Change each character of word from `'a'` to `'z'`; check if mutated word exists in dictionary.
2. **BFS Shortest Path**: Level count of BFS traversal yields shortest sequence length.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `word_ladder_demo()`: Solves Word Ladder shortest transformation sequence using BFS.

projects.title: Course Schedule I & II (Prerequisite Dependency Graph Analysis)
projects.description: Given total courses N and prerequisite pairs `[u, v]` (must take `v` before `u`), determine if you can finish all courses (Course Schedule I) and return a valid course ordering (Course Schedule II). Detect cycles using Topological Sort in O(V + E) time! In this project, you will build Course Schedule Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dependency Graph Modeling, Cycle Detection in Prerequisites & Course Sequence Planning
projects.exampleText: Check course schedule feasibility and print valid course order
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Course Schedule I & II (Prerequisite Dependency Graph) ---
Can finish all 4 courses: YES
Valid course order: [ 0, 1, 2, 3 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Build DAG**: Construct directed adjacency list from prerequisites.
2. **Topological Order**: If topological sort contains all N courses, return order; else return empty (cycle exists).
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `course_schedule_demo()`: Solves Course Schedule I & II using Topological Sort.

projects.title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix (8-Directional Grid BFS)
projects.description: Given an `N x N` binary grid, find the shortest clear path from top-left `(0,0)` to bottom-right `(N-1, N-1)` moving in 8 directions (horizontal, vertical, diagonal). Use 8-directional BFS in O(N^2) time! In this project, you will build 8-Directional Shortest Path BFS in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 8-Directional Grid Moves, Matrix BFS Shortest Paths & Diagonal Grid Traversal
projects.exampleText: Find shortest 8-directional clear path in binary matrix
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Shortest Path in Binary Matrix (8-Directional Grid BFS) ---
Shortest 8-directional clear path length = 4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **8 Neighbors**: Delta vectors `dx = {-1,-1,-1,0,0,1,1,1}`, `dy = {-1,0,1,-1,1,-1,0,1}`.
2. **BFS Queue**: Track path distance per cell.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `shortest_path_binary_matrix_demo()`: Solves shortest path in binary matrix using 8-directional BFS.

projects.title: Is Graph Bipartite? (DFS Graph Coloring)
projects.description: Verify if an undirected graph is Bipartite using DFS 2-Coloring. Traverse disconnected graph components using recursive DFS, coloring adjacent nodes with opposing colors. Returns false if color conflict encountered in O(V + E) time! In this project, you will build Bipartite DFS Verifier in C.
projects.learningOutcome: DFS 2-Coloring, Odd Cycle Detection & Component Bipartite Verification
projects.exampleText: Verify graph 2-colorability via recursive DFS
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Is Graph Bipartite? (DFS Graph Coloring) ---
DFS 2-Coloring Check -> Graph Bipartite: YES
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **DFS Coloring**: Color node `u` with color 1, neighbors with color 2.
2. **Odd Cycle Proof**: A graph is bipartite if and only if it contains NO odd-length cycles.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bipartite_dfs_demo()`: Validates graph bipartite property using DFS.

projects.title: Find Eventual Safe States (Terminal Node Cycle Detection)
projects.description: A node is a 'safe state' if every possible path starting from that node leads to a terminal node (node with no outgoing edges). Nodes that enter a directed cycle are UNSAFE. Reverse graph edges and run BFS (or run 3-Color DFS) to locate all safe nodes in O(V + E) time! In this project, you will build Eventual Safe States Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Reverse Graph Traversals, Terminal Node Reachability & Safe State Detection
projects.exampleText: Locate safe state nodes in directed graph
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Find Eventual Safe States (Terminal Node Cycle Detection) ---
Safe Node Indices: [ 2, 4, 5, 6 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Reverse Graph Edges**: Invert directed edge directions `u -> v` to `v -> u`.
2. **Kahn's BFS Sweep**: Process terminal nodes with outdegree 0; nodes reachable without cycle are safe.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `eventual_safe_states_demo()`: Solves Eventual Safe States using reverse graph BFS.

projects.title: Reconstruct Itinerary (Eulerian Path Hierholzer's Algorithm)
projects.description: Given airline tickets `[from, to]`, reconstruct itinerary starting from 'JFK' using ALL tickets exactly once (Eulerian Path). If multiple itineraries exist, choose lexicographically smallest one. Use Hierholzer's Post-Order DFS Algorithm in `O(E log E)` time! In this project, you will build Eulerian Path Itinerary Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Eulerian Path Algorithms, Hierholzer's Post-Order DFS & Lexicographical Edge Selection
projects.exampleText: Reconstruct Eulerian path flight itinerary from 'JFK'
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Reconstruct Itinerary (Eulerian Path Hierholzer's Algorithm) ---
Eulerian Path Itinerary: [ 'JFK', 'MUC', 'LHR', 'SFO', 'SJC' ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Sorted Edges**: Sort destination lists lexicographically.
2. **Hierholzer DFS**: Follow edges recursively, remove visited edges, push node to itinerary stack upon exiting node.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `reconstruct_itinerary_demo()`: Solves Reconstruct Itinerary using Hierholzer's Eulerian path algorithm.

projects.title: Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) Graph Storage Engine
projects.description: High-performance graph analytics frameworks (GraphX, Gunrock) store massive billion-edge graphs using Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) representation (`row_ptr` and `col_ind` arrays), eliminating pointer overhead for maximum CPU cache hit rates! In this project, you will build CSR Graph Storage Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) Storage, Pointerless Graph Layouts & CPU Cache Hit Maximization
projects.exampleText: Store 100,000 graph edges in contiguous CSR arrays
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) Graph Storage Engine ---
Stored 100,000 graph edges in contiguous CSR `row_ptr` and `col_ind` arrays for 0-overhead CPU cache hits.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **row_ptr Array**: `row_ptr[i]` stores starting offset index of node `i`'s neighbors in `col_ind`.
2. **col_ind Array**: Contiguous array storing all neighbor vertex IDs.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `csr_graph_demo()`: Implements Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) graph storage engine.

projects.title: Parallel Multi-Threaded Breadth-First Search Engine
projects.description: Supercomputing graph engines execute BFS over 1,000,000 nodes concurrently across multi-core processors using Direction-Optimized Parallel BFS (switching between Top-Down push and Bottom-Up pull frontiers) in C! In this project, you will build Parallel Multi-Threaded BFS in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Direction-Optimized Parallel BFS, Multi-Threaded Frontier Expansion & Atomic Swaps
projects.exampleText: Traverse 1M graph nodes across 8 CPU threads via parallel BFS
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Parallel Multi-Threaded Breadth-First Search Engine ---
Traversed 1,000,000 graph nodes using parallel frontier expansion across 8 CPU threads.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Top-Down Push**: Active frontier threads push unvisited neighbors onto next frontier.
2. **Bottom-Up Pull**: Unvisited nodes search incoming edges for active frontier nodes.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `parallel_bfs_demo()`: Solves parallel multi-threaded BFS graph traversal.

projects.title: Tarjan's Bridge and Articulation Point Finder (Low-Link Graph DFS)
projects.description: Find all Bridges (critical edges whose removal disconnects the graph) and Articulation Points (critical nodes) in an undirected graph in single O(V + E) DFS pass using Tarjan's Low-Link values `low[u] = min(discovery[u], discovery[v])`! In this project, you will build Tarjan's Bridge Finder in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Tarjan's Low-Link Graph Algorithm, Bridge & Articulation Point Proofs & Single-Pass DFS
projects.exampleText: Find bridges and articulation points in graph
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Tarjan's Bridge and Articulation Point Finder ---
Bridges Found: [ (1, 2) ]
Articulation Points Found: [ 1 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Discovery & Low Time**: Track node discovery time `tin[u]` and lowest reachable time `low[u]`.
2. **Bridge Proof**: Edge `(u, v)` is a bridge if `low[v] > tin[u]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `tarjan_bridges_demo()`: Identifies bridges and articulation points using Tarjan's low-link algorithm.

projects.title: SIMD-Accelerated Adjacency Bitset Graph Intersection Kernel
projects.description: High-speed graph analytics engines (Triangle Counting, Community Detection) intersect graph neighbor sets using 256-bit AVX2 SIMD bitwise AND operations over adjacency bitsets, evaluating 256 neighbor connections per clock cycle! In this project, you will build SIMD Graph Kernel in C.
projects.learningOutcome: SIMD AVX2 Graph Bitsets, 256-Bit Parallel Intersections & High-Speed Triangle Counting
projects.exampleText: Intersect graph neighbor bitsets via 256-bit AVX2 SIMD
projects.exampleOutput:
--- SIMD-Accelerated Adjacency Bitset Graph Intersection Kernel ---
Intersected graph neighbor sets using 256-bit AVX2 SIMD bitwise AND in 1 clock cycle.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Adjacency Bitmask**: Store neighbor connections as 256-bit bitmask blocks.
2. **SIMD Intersect**: Perform `_mm256_and_si256()` to compute common neighbors instantly.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `simd_graph_intersection_demo()`: Solves SIMD accelerated graph neighbor set intersections.

projects.title: High-Throughput Memory-Mapped Real-Time Graph Traversal Kernel
projects.description: Real-time social graph engines (Twitter, LinkedIn graph search) process 5,000,000 graph traversal queries per second by memory-mapping graph binary files (`mmap`) into system memory buffers with zero copy overhead. In this project, you will build Real-Time Graph Kernel in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Memory-Mapped Graph Files, Zero-Copy Graph Traversals & Microsecond Social Search
projects.exampleText: Process 5M real-time graph traversal queries/sec
projects.exampleOutput:
--- High-Throughput Memory-Mapped Real-Time Graph Traversal Kernel ---
Processed 5,000,000 real-time social network graph traversal queries per second.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Zero-Copy Memory Map**: Map graph CSR file into virtual address space via `mmap`.
2. **High-Throughput Queries**: Traverse graph edges directly from RAM address offsets.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `stream_graph_kernel_demo()`: Simulates high-throughput memory-mapped real-time graph traversal kernel.
